column1: # Golden corpus for the ingredient parser — item 4 of docs/shopping-parser.md.
# Tab-separated:  line <TAB> quantity <TAB> unit <TAB> name <TAB> qualifier
# An empty unit or qualifier is an empty field. Blank lines and # are ignored.
# A line starting with ~ is a KNOWN GAP: the expectation is what the parser
# *should* produce, and it currently doesn't. The test asserts these still
# fail, so fixing one tells you to promote it rather than passing silently.
# Adding a case is one line. That is the whole point — every other item on
# the list is a heuristic, and heuristics regress each other.
# --- fractions, unicode and ascii, and ranges -----------------------------
1 (15 oz) can black beans, drained and rinsed
# --- the same amount restated, without the parentheses (item 5) -----------
# --- the garlic family, which people write four ways ----------------------
# --- descriptors that should not survive into the name --------------------
# --- descriptors that are part of the identity and must survive -----------
# KNOWN GAPS — the expectation is right, the parser isn't there yet.
# Item 6 — alternatives. First one wins, the rest is a note.
# An amount on both sides, in the same system — so item 5 leaves it alone
# (it's a choice, not a conversion) and item 6 inherits it. Today the second
# amount ends up inside the name, which is why this is a gap and not settled.
~1 lb chicken thighs or 2 lb beef
# Item 7 — an instruction wearing an ingredient's clothes.
~1 tablespoon of all purpose flour dissolve in 1/4 cup water
# Two ingredients on one line. Splitting them is its own change.
# "juice of 1 lemon" works; its sibling doesn't.
